task: Implement UI safeguards after AI Adoption tab/page retirement: bookmark redirects, stale localStorage cleanup, and fallback rendering for saved custom dashboard widgets referencing removed adoption metrics.

key_reasoning.reason: Four distinct components across the full UI stack: router.tsx (loader redirect for retired settings route), AnalyticsPage/AnalyticsDashboard (tab-level redirect + retirement notice for ?tab=adoption), useInitialDataFetch hook (localStorage cleanup), and DynamicWidget (retired metricType guard). Each is independently scoped but all must land together to close the retirement safely.

The widget fallback is the most novel piece — DynamicWidget has no existing precedent for dispatching on metricType (only widgetType), so a constant set of six retired strings and a guard before the switch are genuinely new patterns. The localStorage key scope distinction (bare key vs. userId-prefixed compound key) is a subtle correctness risk. Additionally, the acceptance criteria enumerate five specific edge/error/variant cases (bookmark redirect, settings redirect, notice display, localStorage cleanup, widget fallback) and no existing test template covers any of these defensive patterns — triggering the auto-bump from M to L.

Four distinct layers touched: Router (src/router.tsx navigation/redirect), UI (analytics page components and DynamicWidget rendering), Service (useInitialDataFetch app-level hook), and Storage/Persistence (localStorage removeItem for the retired codemie-ai-adoption-config key). Includes persistence operations even without a schema migration.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M(3) to L(4): acceptance criteria enumerate five specific edge/error/variant cases (bookmark redirects, localStorage cleanup, widget fallback notice) with no existing test templates covering any of these defensive patterns.
